messages:
Alex: anyone else seeing a spike in pending GPU pods in us-west2b?
Maya: yup, noticed ~120 pending since ~10:05. scheduler keeps requeuing the same gang jobs.
Ben: checked scheduler logs — a lot of "Fit failure: NodeAffinity mismatch" and "Insufficient GPUs" entries.
Maya: this started right after yesterday's provisioning rollback. the reserved pool in us-west2b never came fully back.
Alex: also saw a network change around 09:50 — eBPF update touched kube-proxy configs. could be conntrack related causing node readiness flaps.
Ben: kubectl describe on a pending shows taints: gpu-reserved=true:NoSchedule and the pods don't tolerate that (they had nodeSelector us-west2b).
Maya: hmm, some jobdefs set tolerationSeconds=60 — I thought that only affects eviction?
Ben: yeah normally, but the descheduler uses that to decide when to evict and reschedule; combined with preemptions it's compounding.
Chris: infra-bot: Auto-scaler attempted scale-up for reserved-pool-usw2b at 10:07 but failed: quotaExceeded (GPU quota).
Maya: so autoscaler couldn't add nodes, scheduler kept piling up pendings, then started preempting tiny pods in other AZs to try to satisfy gangs. chain reaction.
Alex: what's the risk of temporarily relaxing the nodeSelector/topologySpread so these jobs can land in other AZs? data-locality might suffer.
Sanjay: spreading across AZs will increase cross-AZ egress and cost. need finance/product sign-off if sustained. :money_with_wings:
Maya: proposed immediate playbook: 1) request GPU quota bump from cloud 2) remove hard nodeSelector on non-critical canaries 3) revert/roll back eBPF change if correlation confirmed 4) add a scheduler backfill ratio to allow partial gang placement (best-effort fallback).
Alex: I'll push a canary that adds preferredDuringScheduling (weight 50) allowing usa-west fallback. Maya can open quota ticket.
Ben: after the canary, ~30 pods scheduled across us-west2a and us-west2c, but we saw more preemptions in us-west2a — taint propagation and preempt windows intersecting.
Maya: infra-bot created INC-2026-0042 for tracking.
Chris: infra-bot: checkpoint — autoscaler logs indicate it treats nodes in state 'drained' as unschedulable and didn't attempt scale-out due to a precondition check.
Maya: that's a bug: drained pool should be considered for scale-up if pool-autoscaler can reprovision, not just ignored.
Alex: action items agreed:
- Maya: open quota request and cloud support ticket (done: TICKET-9221)
- Alex: roll canary removing hard nodeSelector for train-large (prefers, not requires)
- Ben: gather scheduler traces + fit/failure histogram and attach to the incident
- Infra: revert eBPF change only if we get a clear signal; otherwise throttle/rollback plan ready
- Product/Finance: confirm temporary cross-AZ cost opt-in by EOD
Ben: tech detail I captured: scheduler output snippet:
```
E1010 10:12:34 scheduler_predicates.go:254] Fit failure for pod train-large-7: node(s) didn't match NodeSelector, node(s) had taint gpu-reserved=true:NoSchedule
E1010 10:13:42 predicate_checker.go:98] Insufficient GPUs: requested 4, available 0 on node gke-usw2b-pool-3
```
Maya: rolling the canary now — will monitor for preempts and latency.
Alex: watching. if we don't see stabilization in 30m we'll enact quota bump as emergency.
Sanjay: FYI, long-term we need: pool-provision-health metric, autoscaler precondition tweak (treat 'drained' separately), and a cost-aware scheduling policy toggle for emergencies.
Maya: adding postmortem note: provisioning rollback left pool in 'drained' state but taint remained. autoscaler misinterpreted that and refused scale-up. fix: add pool-state tag to autoscaler logic + alert on drained+tainted mismatch.
Ben: will upload traces + k8s event dump to the incident doc.
Alex: thanks all — keeping this thread as the live incident channel.
Maya: update at +20: more pods scheduled, preempts reduced. reverting canary if no regressions.
Sanjay: pinging finance for temporary approval.
Chris: infra-bot: incident updated INC-2026-0042 -> pager duty escalation level 2.
Alex: good work. postmortem owners: Maya (infra), Ben (scheduler), Alex (runbook).
Maya: closing loop: will draft postmortem template after incident stabilizes.
